metadata.title: Alphabet Jumps 2.5% After Locking In 22 Years of Nuclear Power

content.text:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.
Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOGL), Google's search, cloud and artificial-intelligence parent, pledged at least 13 billion, or roughly $15.1 billion, for a massive AI infrastructure push in Finland. The stock climbed approximately 2.5% to $338.67 Friday morning as investors weighed another aggressive bet on the computing power behind Google's next growth cycle.
The two-year buildout spans data centers, grid upgrades, renewable energy and battery storage, Reuters reported. Google also secured the right to buy up to half the electricity generated by a Fortum nuclear plant under a 22-year agreement. That long runway matters: Gemini, Search, Maps and YouTube need dependable power at enormous scale, and Alphabet is locking it in before AI demand accelerates further.
Finland expects construction to add 3.6 billion to economic output, while the completed infrastructure could support 7,000 jobs annually. Investors should keep that economic benefit separate from Alphabet's own returnsthe real test is whether cloud and advertising growth can earn back the heavy capital spending. The chart adds a valuation warning: at $338.67, the shares trade 33.77% above their $253.17 GF Value, leaving little room for disappointing returns on this AI expansion.
